summary:
ASTRA HEALTH is an AI-assisted spaceflight health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to support astronaut health and safety during long-duration space missions. The system brings together space-health research, physiological indicators, and intelligent analysis to help identify potential health risks and support timely decision-making.

The platform provides health monitoring dashboards, risk assessment, explainable alerts, historical trend analysis, and AI-powered health insights. It is designed with an offline-first approach to support environments where continuous internet connectivity is unavailable.

By combining NASA space-health research with modern AI and data analytics, ASTRA HEALTH aims to make complex health information easier to interpret, improve situational awareness, and support safer human space exploration.
details:
ASTRA HEALTH is an intelligent health-monitoring and decision-support platform designed to address the challenges of maintaining astronaut health during space missions, particularly long-duration missions where medical assistance and communication with Earth may be limited.

Repo: https://github.com/Kartikey455001/Astra-Health

How It Works

The platform combines space-health research, physiological indicators, and AI-assisted analysis to provide a centralized view of astronaut health. It includes:

  • Health Monitoring Dashboard: Displays physiological indicators and health-related information.
  • AI Health Analysis: Analyzes available health information and generates understandable insights.
  • Risk Assessment: Identifies potential health risks and highlights abnormal trends.
  • Explainable Alerts: Provides alerts with supporting context to help users understand potential concerns.
  • Historical Analysis: Tracks health trends over time to support better decisions.
  • AI Health Assistant: Helps interpret health information and provides relevant explanations.
  • Offline-First Architecture: Designed to remain useful in environments with limited or unavailable internet connectivity.

NASA Data Integration

ASTRA HEALTH uses NASA space-health research resources, including the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA), NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), and relevant space-weather information from DONKI. These resources provide scientific context for understanding the challenges of human health and safety in space.

Technology Stack

Frontend: React, Vite, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Recharts.

Backend: Node.js, Express.js, Socket.IO.

AI/ML: Python, FastAPI, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, Gemini API, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

Database: PostgreSQL, Supabase, Prisma, pgvector.

Deployment: Vercel, Render, Docker, Progressive Web App (PWA), Service Workers and IndexedDB.

Innovation and Impact

The key innovation is bringing space-health research, AI-assisted interpretation, explainable risk indicators, and offline accessibility into one platform. ASTRA HEALTH aims to improve health awareness, support early identification of potential concerns, and contribute to safer human exploration of the Moon and Mars.

The prototype uses simulated or manually supplied physiological indicators where real astronaut telemetry is unavailable. It is a research and decision-support prototype, not a replacement for professional medical diagnosis.
